scores.concept: ONE ISLAND, ONE TAP — the void's window
scores.notes: Best for a non-reader: picture pips (burger/basket/hero emoji/crown/globe), picture tabs (🛍️ / void face / 📗), tap-the-void = chomp = the audio-unlock gesture, locked pip = wiggle with no text. Two flow faults cost it the win: (1) CONTINUE after a win goes to the MENU, not the next level (#btnAgain -> btnHome path :7696-7702), so every level cycle is win -> CONTINUE -> menu -> PLAY = two taps plus an enterMenu warp/re-park, against 2 and 3 which put CONTINUE straight into the next pip via resetMatch (:7571); (2) NO fail-forward — within a world pips are strictly sequential with no 3-miss release, so a six-year-old who cannot cross LANDMARK (worlds 2-5 cross the hero threshold only inside the finale surge, :1553-1555; lawCap :9746-9748) is walled at pip 3 of that world with pips 4-5 dead, exactly the unlocks.ts:8-16 case, only softened by the next world opening on finish. Composition fault: a 360-degree orbit around the void at 28 units (90 s/turn, wall clock) keeps him centred but swings the waterfall/landmark/family behind the camera half the time, so 'island above, void below' is true at one azimuth only; the Maple stage at the waterfall lip (190,207.5) is the plateau RIM (island.ts:278, :3812) — off-island sky for half the turn and unverified as standable ground. Perf: hard commit to shadows OFF on every menu entry via the intro toggle (:10505-10509) makes the close diorama flat and puts the first-toggle recompile (AUDIT-2026-08-23.md:316) on the menu's first frame; DPR 1.5, bloom off, absolute draw-call bar <=1,400 and 20 s idle throttle are the most concrete numbers of the three. Moves BY MYSELF into #settings (not an owner decision; solotog.mjs re-point). 15.5 crew-days with six authored MENU_STAGE coordinates that need a lookbook before anyone can say they frame.

scores.concept: Splash Alive — the living island menu with the five-bite ladder
scores.notes: The flow a parent wants: PLAY is one tap, CONTINUE is the next pip with no menu round-trip, a miss says NOT YET with the frozen counter and pays the coins anyway, the third miss opens the next pip ('...or try level 4') so nothing walls her, RIVALS always deals the family, Skylark's whale is named only if qa/pace.mjs proves it reachable. Most character of the three: chomp+smug on tap, hungry on PLAY, scared blink on a locked pip, pupils on the pointer (void3d.ts:54-75, :2340-2347). Closest camera (22 units, pendulum ±6 deg over 16 s) = the cheapest frame and the biggest face (~65 px at FOV 32, :663). Harsh marks: identity 3 because it is Hole.io's skeleton AND Hole.io's paint — flat #4c3cbe ground, blue/violet/orange tabs — a parent who has seen Hole.io reads 'reskin' in the first second, and the recon numbers were a measurement, not an owner decision to copy the palette; tab icons are unspecified (labels only), and 'FINISH LEVEL 2 FIRST' / the 18 px goal line are text a six-year-old cannot read. The shrunk logo floating INSIDE the diorama window over a moving sky steals window pixels and makes firstframe --splash (firstframe.mjs:215-220) non-deterministic; the L4 'family stands 6 units behind the void' quietly requires warping and posing rivals, which is unscoped. Perf 3: the plan measures (0.5 day) but is the least defensive — shadows left 'whatever the renderer has', no adaptive fallback on the menu, idle throttle only at 45 s, no compile pre-warm — it relies on the close frame being cheap, which is plausible but is exactly the unmeasured claim. Cheapest build (13.5 days) with the tightest probe list (house 4.5:1, taps=1 on /?manual=1, ratio <=1.15).

scores.concept: LIVING SPLASH — the key art rendered live, five pips under it, one tap to play
scores.notes: The best answer to 'make our splash image alive': our dark-violet cosmos with a feathered oval window so the island FLOATS, the void looking UP at the landmark with autonomous gaze-up and chomp beats every 6-14 s, post-HOME camera eases 900 ms into the orbit, the daily-card condition rewrite (:7967) and the pickerfit/firstframe 'throw if absent' guards land in S0 before anything moves. But it is the worst screen for a six-year-old's hands and eyes: pips are 36 px (below the 44 pt tap minimum; 1 and 2 use 44/57), numbered 1-5 with no picture of the goal, three DARK tabs (teal #124a5c / violet #33175e / plum #5a1d4e) with text labels and no icons — she cannot tell SHOP from BOOK without reading — and the camera at 58 units makes the void ~25 px tall in a 457 px window (FOV 32 deg, :663) — a coin, not a face — while claiming 'face in the lower third'. Perf 3: the most thorough mechanism (3-step menuRung self-degrade, renderer.compile pre-warm, document.hidden gate, 5-min quarter-rate) wrapped around the HOTTEST frame of the three (58-unit wedge, draw-call bar 1.6x settled = ~2,000, crowdGate 218 > today's 200) — it builds a fire escape and then picks the top floor. Internal contradiction: a 'stolen' fail state ('THE FAMILY GOT THERE FIRST') AND heroProp excluded from rival bites on level 3 — one of those is dead code. Retires the gate's questable step (gate.mjs:406) before qa/levels.mjs exists to replace the supply count — the GOVERNOR.md:148 bug class. Most expensive (16.5 days) with the optional water stream and book re-parenting of #trophies/#topvoids.

winner: Splash Alive — the living island menu with the five-bite ladder
grafts_from_runners_up: From ONE ISLAND: drop Hole.io's paint. Keep Splash Alive's band proportions (49% window / 45% ground) but paint the ground with #menu's existing radial violet (#33175e -> #1c0f3d -> #0d0821) and ::before star dots (index.html:885-896), and from LIVING SPLASH cut the window as a feathered ellipse (mask-image, ~48 px feather) so the island floats in the cosmos like the key art; tab hues become ours (keep three distinct BRIGHT hues, not LIVING SPLASH's three darks) with pairwise deltaE >= 15 kept as the bar.

From ONE ISLAND: picture tabs — SHOP 🛍️ / HOME = the void's face glyph / SCRAPBOOK 📗 at 28 px with 11 px labels (index.html:1976-1977 ids kept) — Splash Alive specifies labels only; a six-year-old picks tabs by picture.

From ONE ISLAND: move the logo OUT of the diorama window into its own band above it (band B, 40 px cap height) instead of floating it over the live sky; keeps '#menu .logo' / '#menu .logo i' deterministic for firstframe --splash (firstframe.mjs:215-220) and gives the window back its top 50 px. Trim the safe-area band to keep the window at 49%.

From ONE ISLAND: the menu-side pip HOP on re-entry (finished pip flips grey/magenta in 180 ms, then the green ring hops one right in 220 ms with audio.ready()) for whenever the child returns via HOME rather than CONTINUE — Splash Alive only animates the pip on the end card.

From ONE ISLAND: idle throttle at 20 s (not 45 s) and an ABSOLUTE draw-call bar (<= 1,400 at the parked camera per world, settled-play class :10496-10500) printed alongside the menu/match ratio, plus life.moverStats(gate) per world (life.ts:6906) — the owner reads numbers.

From LIVING SPLASH: the 3-step menu-only degrade (menuRung in __menuState, never written to qLevel: DPR 1.0 -> shadows off via the intro toggle :10505-10509 -> frozen orbit at half-rate with dt doubled for island.update) and the document.hidden no-render gate on the rAF (:10957) — the only mechanism that reacts to a device number nobody has yet.

From LIVING SPLASH: renderer.compile() pre-warm at boot under the cover, made CONDITIONAL on S0 measuring a first-toggle recompile stall (AUDIT-2026-08-23.md:316); and the post-HOME 900 ms camera ease from the match position into the pendulum instead of a cut.

From LIVING SPLASH: the autonomous character beats — gaze-up at the landmark every 6-9 s for 1.4 s (lookX/lookY) and a chomp(0.6) every 14 s preceded by 0.8 s of 'hungry' via the rig API — so the diorama has a character even when nobody is tapping; Splash Alive's void only reacts.

From LIVING SPLASH: land the pickerfit.mjs:245-260 / firstframe.mjs:220 'throw if absent' guards and teach firstframe's freeze() to keep the canvas in S0, before the menu changes — not in the migration step at the end; and the explicit daily-card condition check at :7967.

From LIVING SPLASH: keep 'LEVEL n OF 30' off the menu (Splash Alive already does) and cut the L4 'family stands behind the void' pose from Splash Alive — freeze AND hide the rivals on the menu; the family belongs in the match, not the postcard.
what_all_three_missed: The post-HOME menu shows a half-eaten island. #btnHome (prototype3d.ts:7696-7701) only removes #end.show, sets body.menu, menuEl.style.display='' and renderRank(); it never calls resetMatch() (:7571), which is the ONLY path that restores eaten edibles (e.eaten=false; e.mesh.visible=true at resetMatch +53..57) and resets the void (voidling.setStage(0); voidling.setRadius(START_R) at +74). So after any match the 'diorama of the current level' is a crater where the Town Hall / Royal Mariner / Stadium was, with a match-sized void (up to R 12) parked in front of it, and the boot menu and the post-HOME menu look like two different games. enterMenu() must run the restore loop (split out of resetMatch) before parking the camera. All three wrote a state-model paragraph and none read btnHome.

The void's size on the menu is never authored. camera FOV is 32 deg vertical (prototype3d.ts:663), so visible height = 0.574 x distance: at START_R (~0.9, diameter ~1.8 units) the creature is ~65 px tall at 22 units, ~51 px at 28, ~25 px at 58, in a 457 px window — a coin, not the key art's face that fills ~40% of the frame. Every concept asserts 'face in the lower third' with no arithmetic; the rig already exposes setRadius (void3d.ts:24, :1704) so a menu display radius (e.g. 3-4 units, restored to START_R at leaveMenu) is a one-line authored number nobody wrote down. This also decides whether tap-to-chomp is even hittable.

Reduce-motion is ignored. fx.ts:48-65 reduceMotion()/voidMotion is a shipped setting surfaced as 'big motion' in the pause sheet (:7734-7736); none of the three gates the orbit/pendulum, PLAY breathe, pip ring pulse or the chomp beats on it. A motion-sensitive child, or a parent who turned big motion OFF, gets a permanently moving menu.

Frozen rivals mid-stride. All three freeze rivals.update (:10290) on the menu; none hides the meshes. On the boot menu the family walks today (t=0 branch, rivals.ts:852-863) and would freeze the instant the gate lands — a walker locked mid-step inside a scene where the crowd keeps working reads as a bug. Same class: fadeOccluders is switched off (:10896, :1184-1200) while the camera is moved to a new place, so any tree/prop on the camera-to-void line stays opaque; no concept tests the parked position for clearance.

Only one viewport. Every band table is authored for 430x932 and nothing else, yet the push splash step runs six viewports (gate.mjs:233-236) and firstframe already documents a 393x700 case; on a short phone the 49% window + 64-88 px PLAY + 72-96 px tab bar + pips + logo do not fit and nobody states the collapse order (window shrinks first, tabs shrink, logo goes). Landscape/iPad: silent.

Chips below a child's finger. Season pill 28 px, #soloTog chip 28 px, world chip/plate 26-28 px (and LIVING SPLASH's 36 px pips) are all under the 44 pt minimum; the primary tester is six. Nobody sized a single secondary control for her hand.
No haptic on the one new delight. voidHaptics exists (:3594) and the tap-chomp / pip hop / locked-pip wiggle are the menu's three tactile moments; none of the three fires it.

The SHOP tab is one tap from her thumb and nobody says what she sees there. The parental gate (#gate z70) is on spend, not entry; kids' 4+ apps routinely put a grown-ups shield on store ENTRY, and none of the three states whether the shop shows prices, real-money items, or only coin skins when a six-year-old opens it from the brightest tab on the screen.

The first-ever session never shows the menu (:6559-6562 auto-plays Maple with no menu), so the daughter's first sight of the 'exceptional menu' is after her first match — only LIVING SPLASH mentions it, and none designs that first reveal (the pip row lighting from nothing to 'level 1 done' is the moment the whole ladder is sold).
